question: When a superclaude launch finds its instance already held by a live loop, should it (a) refuse, naming the live loop and suggesting --instance=N, (b) move itself to the next free instance automatically, as restart spawn already does, or (c) stay at the same instance with its own per-session loop.pid and flags inside it?
why_it_blocks: Two CC sessions were launched at instance 0 (both --name akiendelllinux_cc_0) and share one loop.pid and one restart-flag set, so a restart from one can hang up the other. The fix has three shapes meaning different things for what an instance address is, and the proof's teeth differ by the answer. CC recommends (b): it keeps instance = one session, which is what a singleton at 0 means, and matches restart spawn.
answered_by: Akien, recorded by caller class cc
